title: A major standoff-missile award exposes a concentrated but component-diverse subordinate supplier structure
source_unit: USAspending subaward records linked to one DoD JASSM/LRASM parent contract
geography: United States parent award; subordinate recipient locations are not supplied in this extract

reported_recipient_count.unit: distinct recipient names in returned records

observations.method: Single parent-award POST retrieval from the official USAspending subawards endpoint with page size 100; recipient amounts summed across returned records and duplicate recipient names aggregated.
observations.uncertainty: The extract is bounded to one parent award and the endpoint's returned records. Recipient names are not an independently reconciled ownership or legal-entity master; subordinate tiers, locations, unreported records, amendments, and timing outside the returned action dates are not established.
observations.subgroup: Reported subordinate recipients, compared by extract amount; the largest is BAE Systems Information and Electronic Systems Integration Inc., followed by L3Harris Cincinnati Electronics Corporation and Chemring Energetic Devices Inc.
observations.counterinterpretation: A 51-recipient extract may indicate distributed component sourcing, but it can also reflect prime-contract reporting conventions, repeated lots, or incomplete visibility; it does not establish supplier competition, resilience, domestic self-sufficiency, or local economic benefit.

observations.period: 2024-10-23 through 2025-02-28; descriptions attached to returned subaward records

denominator.unit: returned subaward records with free-text descriptions

component_and_assembly_terms_present.unit: records with one or more component/assembly descriptions

examples_of_reported_system_elements.value: warhead cases; inertial measurement units; antennas; engines; mission-control processors; fuzing/electronics; wings, tails, and structural covers; optics; power supplies and connectors

observations.method: Qualitative coding of the returned description strings; examples are retained as text-visible categories and are not a parts list or bill of materials.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptions are abbreviated procurement text, sometimes repeated across lots and options, with no quantities, acceptance status, manufacturing location, input provenance, worker count, or delivery confirmation.
observations.subgroup: Reported component and assembly descriptions within one JASSM/LRASM parent-award subaward extract.
observations.counterinterpretation: Component terms show what was reported as procured, not that the component was manufactured, integrated, delivered, or available at the implied scale; the same description can cover testing, support, options, or recurring lots.

boundary: This case record links one parent defense award to reported subordinate recipients, amounts, dates, and description-visible component classes. It does not establish a complete supply chain, ownership, geography, production, delivery, workforce, readiness, resilience, local incidence, or geopolitical leverage.
